gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much AC energy any of these 1 kWh kits actually delivered in a named test. OutdoorGearLab (one editor, one method) measured 950 Wh from the BLUETTI AC180, 910 Wh from the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 and 890 Wh from the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2, and StorageReview measured 910 Wh from the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus. All the rivals use an assumed 85% instead.
standout_why: I opened the three cited rival pages. StormWatts (2026-11-08) says it ran no hands-on tests: it lists maker capacities and uses 85% as a planning assumption. Its only real measurement is one owner test of a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus, which is a different class. Trek4Tech (2026-09-05) says 'We did not test any of these units' and shows about 85% usable as an unexplained estimate. SolutionEnergy (2026-11-08) relays maker specs and its own estimate that about 85% of rated capacity is usable. None of the three names a reviewer or lab measurement for any candidate. theoutageplan.com (cited in chat 2) would not open (self-signed certificate error), so I could not check it. ChatGPT's own answer also says '850–900Wh usable' with no source.
decides: This confirms the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and AC180 as the 1 kWh value kits on measured energy, not just on price. At the link price, the AC180 + 200 W kit costs $730.55 for 950 measured Wh ($0.77 per measured Wh). The Elite 100 V2 + 200 W kit costs $692.55 for 890 measured Wh ($0.78 per measured Wh). The Pioneer Na + 200 W kit costs $949.05 for about 774 Wh, worked out from The Solar Lab's 86% efficiency figure ($1.23 per Wh). That makes it the weakest on measured energy per dollar, although it is one of our kits that ships now. Both the AC180 and Elite 100 V2 kits are pre-orders (Dec 14 and mid-December 2026), so the measurements support naming them as the cheaper option for a shopper who can wait, not as the ship-now pick. The measured gaps between the 1 kWh stations are small (890–950 Wh), so measured energy does not overturn a pick on its own. It does show that the AC180's larger 1,152 Wh nameplate turns into about 40–60 more usable Wh than the 1,024–1,070 Wh rivals. The Anker C1000 Gen 2 is rated 2,000 W AC, which is outside the 1,000–1,800 W line. Its measurements are listed for context only.
candidates: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 + 200 W (2,000 W AC, outside the 1,000–1,800 W line)

findings.label: Measured AC energy out (full discharge)
findings.source_title: OutdoorGearLab – BLUETTI AC180 review (Kenji Mowrey, published 2026-01-13)
findings.note: Quote: 'Our testers measured 950 Wh, which is 18% below its advertised 1,152 Wh.' The page does not state the test load. Same lab and editor as the Jackery 1000 v2 and Elite 100 V2 rows.

findings.label: Solar refill with one 200 W panel (reviewer's field result)
findings.value: Full charge in 6–8 hours under ideal conditions
findings.note: Quote: 'Using just one 200 watt panel, we could achieve a full charge in 6-8 hours under ideal conditions.' No logged wattage, and the panel model is not named. For comparison, 1,152 Wh ÷ 200 W at rated output = 5.8 h.

findings.label: Measured AC energy out (full discharge)

findings.note: Quote: 'we measured 890 Wh out of its advertised 1,024 Wh.' Load not detailed. The same page measured AC charging at 512 Wh/hr (about 2 h from 0%) and the unit's weight at 25.0 lb.

findings.label: Measured AC energy out at a constant 500 W load
findings.value: 946 Wh (about 93% of 1,024 Wh); about 80% at loads in the double-digit watts

findings.label: Measured energy in/out and noise
findings.value: 1,020 Wh taken in from the wall, 902 Wh used; about 47 dB charging/discharging, about 30 dB in quiet charge mode (about 260 W)

findings.label: Measured discharge and recharge, 100%→0%→100%
findings.value: 910 Wh out (88.9% of 1,024 Wh); 1,180 Wh in to refill (86.8% recharge efficiency); UPS transfer just over 8 ms
findings.source_title: StorageReview – EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus review (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-01-02)
findings.note: Discharge load not stated. The UPS transfer time was measured with a Quarch Mains Power Analysis Module against the maker's 10 ms rating.

findings.label: Measured efficiency (sodium-ion)

findings.source_title: The Solar Lab – Bluetti Pioneer Na review (no author or date on the page)

findings.label: Measured AC energy out at a constant 1 kW load; idle draw; noise
